heroSub: 9 hand-picked Koh Sichang stays we've reviewed in depth — the blue-and-white Cape & Kantary boutique resort, a clifftop bungalow where every room's balcony faces the sunset, a yellow house on the cliffside, down to a small in-town guesthouse within walking distance of the pier. From about ฿800–1,900/night.
introH2: 🏝️ What kinds of stays does Koh Sichang have, and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: Koh Sichang is a small island off Sriracha that Bangkok folks love escaping to for the weekend, since the ferry across takes only about 45 minutes and you get the feel of a quiet island that isn't crowded like Pattaya — and that's exactly what makes choosing a stay here worth a little thought, because each type plays a different angle on "location." · Some are seaside boutique resorts selling design and views, some are clifftop bungalows with balconies facing the sunset, some are small in-town guesthouses within walking distance of the pier and restaurants. · Plenty of people book a clifftop stay for the pretty view and only then find out there are lots of stairs to climb, or book a place in the middle of the village and end up disappointed it isn't beachfront. · This article rounds up 9 places to stay on Koh Sichang that we've reviewed in depth — every one drawn from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, with both the upsides and the honest caveats, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Koh Sichang has no major roads or city-style public transport. Getting there starts with driving or taking a car to Koh Loy Pier, Sriracha (about 1.5–2 hours from Bangkok), then boarding the ferry that runs on set departures — the fare is around 50 baht and the crossing takes about 45 minutes. · You don't need to bring your own car onto the island; just park on the Sriracha side. · On the island, most people rent a skylab three-wheeler or a motorbike to get around, making it easy to stop at Chong Khao Khat, Phra Chudadhuj Palace, the Chao Pho Khao Yai Shrine, and Tham Phang Beach. · The stay zones in this article: seaside / clifftop — pretty views and quiet, but some require walking up a hill or stairs · in the village near the pier — within walking distance of the market and restaurants, handy for heading out. · Check the schedule for the last ferry carefully, especially on long weekends when boats can get crowded.

entries.name: Somewhere Koh Sichang
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Thewawong · about 5 min from the pier
tags: 🌊 Every room's balcony has a sea view
entries.addr: 194/1 Moo 3, Tha Thewawong Sub-district, Koh Sichang, Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: If there's one stay on Koh Sichang that people talk about most for its design and the care behind it, plenty of reviews give it to this one — Somewhere Koh Sichang is a small boutique resort of just 20 rooms in the Cape & Kantary Hotels group, set on a hill in Tha Thewawong Sub-district. It's been open since 2016 and had a major renovation in 2022, so the rooms and common areas still look fresh. It holds the highest score in this article at 9.6 from 96 reviews on Trip.com, plus a Travelers' Choice 2026 from TripAdvisor. · What makes people fall for it is the blue-and-white nautical palette across the whole building, which has become a popular photo spot, and the fact that every room has a private balcony with chairs to sit and relax — upper-floor rooms face the sea for a wide bay view with cargo ships moored in the distance as a backdrop, while ground-floor rooms look onto the pool and garden. · What reviews agree on most is the service: several staff are named and praised personally, both the shuttle driver and the front-desk team, who look after you with the care of staying at a relative's place. There's a free shuttle from the island pier plus parking on the Sriracha side, which genuinely solves the headache of finding transport on the island. · For food, The Veerandah restaurant serves both Thai and international dishes, with well-made Thai food and a semi-buffet breakfast cooked to order that draws praise. · Honest caveats from the reviews: it's a small resort, so bathroom amenities like shampoo and soap are sometimes a little sparse, cleanliness in some rooms isn't consistent, dinner options are limited because it's away from the village, and if a sea view matters to you, you'll need to request an upper-floor room at booking. · This is a stay you pay for the atmosphere and peace of mind more than for luxury — good for couples and small families wanting a quiet one-night seaside trip.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request an upper-floor sea-facing room at the time of booking, because ground-floor rooms look onto the pool and garden instead — the sea view from the balcony is the highlight you shouldn't miss. · And pack your own shampoo and soap just in case, since reviews say they're given sparingly.
pros: Highest score in the article at 9.6 · pretty blue-and-white design, renovated 2022
Every room has a balcony; upper-floor rooms with wide sea views are the highlight reviews praise
Cape & Kantary-group service is attentive, with a free pier shuttle
Sea-view pool and the Thai food at The Veerandah draw praise
cons: It's a small boutique, so bathroom amenities are sparse — bring your own
Dinner options are limited because it's away from the village
Ground-floor rooms look onto the pool and garden, not a full sea view (per reviews)

entries.name: Koh Sichang Unseen
entries.badge: 🌅 Every room's balcony faces the sunset
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Thewawong · on the west-side cliff
tags: 🌅 Every room's balcony faces the sea
🏖️ Private beach, see the cave at low tide
entries.addr: 122 Moo 2, Tha Thewawong Sub-district, Koh Sichang, Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: If a sunset view is what you're after on a Koh Sichang trip, Koh Sichang Unseen is the name many reviews bring up — a small bungalow resort of just 12 rooms perched on a seaside cliff on the island's west side. It's been open since around 2015, with a score of 9.1 from 47 reviews on Trip.com. · The selling point that sets it apart from other stays on the island is that nearly every room has a balcony facing the sea — the Sea View rooms at 28–30 sqm have windows looking out to sea on two or three sides, so it feels like you're truly sleeping by the water, and in the evening you can sit and watch the sun set into the sea right in front of your own room without having to go anywhere. · Another highlight is the small private beach below the resort, with a path down to a rocky shore and seaside boulders — a quiet spot for sitting and taking photos — and at low tide you can see the cave and rock hollows along the shore, a sight you'll only catch at certain times. · Service gets consistent praise: staff are friendly and help carry luggage up and down the stairs, breakfast is included in the room rate, and there's free parking on the Sriracha side for leaving your car while you cross to the island. · Honest caveats from the reviews: the thing mentioned most is the fairly steep stairs up to the rooms, since the resort sits on a cliff — not ideal for anyone who struggles with walking or has heavy luggage. · Next is a smell from the bathroom drains in some rooms, AC that doesn't get cold enough at times, no swimming pool, and breakfast options that are still limited given the small-resort scale. · Best for couples and groups of friends wanting a quiet atmosphere, with the sea view and sunset as the star of the trip.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request a Sea View room facing the sea at the time of booking, because some rooms don't have as open a view as the cliffside front rooms. · If you have elderly travelers or heavy luggage, ask about the stairs and have staff help carry your things from check-in.
pros: Nearly every room's balcony faces the sea — a sunset view from your own room
Has a private beach below, with the cave and rock hollows visible at low tide
Small 12-room resort feels private · breakfast included, free parking on the Sriracha side
Staff are friendly and help carry luggage up the stairs (per reviews)
cons: The stairs up to the rooms are fairly steep — not ideal for those who struggle with walking
No swimming pool · a smell from the drains in some rooms, AC not cold enough at times
Breakfast options are still limited given the small-resort scale (per reviews)

entries.type: In-village bungalow · walk to the pier
entries.name: Benjaporn Bungalow
entries.revCount: Booking 8.8 · 577 reviews · TripAdvisor #2 small stay on the island
entries.badge: 🚐 Lots of reviews · free pier shuttle
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Thewawong · 5–7 min walk to the pier
tags: 🛏️ Clean rooms, beds comfier than the price
🚶 Walk to the pier and market
entries.addr: 72/1 Moo 3, Tha Thewawong Sub-district, Koh Sichang, Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: If you measure by the sheer number of reviews among small stays on Koh Sichang, Benjaporn Bungalow is one of the places with the largest base of guests talking about it — a score of 8.8 on Booking.com, and TripAdvisor 4.5/5 ranking it #2 of the 11 small stays on the island. · It's a small cluster of about 14 bungalows set in the island's village, near the pier, market, and restaurants. Its position is clear: a "budget base" that lets you head out around the island all day and come back to sleep comfortably. · What real reviews agree on most is that the rooms are clean and the beds are wide, soft, and comfier than the price — many say they slept really well, which is the single most important thing for a stay at this price. · Location is a strength too, since it's a 5–7 minute walk to the pier, market, and restaurants, with Phra Chudadhuj Palace an easy walk uphill. · The service that impresses most people is the free shuttle from the island pier, which cuts out the hassle of finding transport on the island, plus a free bike loan, free parking, and a freshly made breakfast of eggs, sausage, ham, and coffee. · The owner and staff are friendly and look after you closely. · Honest caveats from the reviews: it isn't beachfront and has no swimming pool, the design and furniture are simple and basic for the price, the bathroom drainage in some bungalows leaves water pooling on the floor after a shower, the Wi-Fi signal is weak in some rooms (bring a backup SIM), and breakfast is a small set, not as varied as a big hotel. · Best for couples, groups of friends, and small families who want to explore the island on a budget but still want a clean bed and an easy-to-walk location.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Make the most of the free pier shuttle by telling the stay in advance what time you'll reach the pier. · If you want an upper-floor room that catches a bit of sea view or has a balcony, specify the room type at booking, and bring a backup mobile SIM since the Wi-Fi is weak in some rooms.
pros: Lots of reviews — 577 · TripAdvisor #2 small stay on the island
Clean rooms, beds wide, soft, and comfier than the price (the point reviews praise often)
In-village location, a 5–7 min walk to the pier, market, and restaurants
Free pier shuttle, free bike loan, easy-to-reach price
cons: Not beachfront and no swimming pool — meant as a base for exploring
Bathroom drainage in some bungalows is slow · Wi-Fi weak in some rooms
Design and furniture are simple for the price (per reviews)

entries.type: Guest House 2-Star · yellow house on the cliffside
entries.name: Yellow House Koh Sichang
entries.revCount: Agoda 8.8 · over 650 reviews · top-ranked guesthouse on the island
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Thewawong · on the cliff in the island's center
tags: 💛 Kind owner speaks German and English
🍳 Breakfast included, made by the owner
entries.addr: 71/1 Maha Jai Phakdi Road, Tha Thewawong Sub-district, Koh Sichang, Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: On Koh Sichang, when it comes to budget sea-view stays people mention often, one of them is Yellow House Koh Sichang — a small yellow house set on a seaside cliff looking out over the Gulf of Thailand with a full sunset view, in the Tha Thewawong area. It scores around 8.8 on Agoda from over 650 reviews and ranks among the top guesthouses on the island. · To be honest, this isn't a luxury resort — no grand lobby, no swimming pool — but a small guesthouse with just a few rooms looked after like a family home. · What sets it apart from stays at similar prices is that many rooms have a private balcony facing the sea; open the door and you meet a view of the Gulf and the sea breeze, sipping coffee in the morning or waiting for the sunset in the evening from your own room. Rooms have AC, a TV, free Wi-Fi, and an en-suite bathroom. · The heart of its high praise is the kind Thai owner who speaks German and English — a warm welcome, helping arrange motorbike rentals, and recommending restaurants and island spots like a local friend, plus a breakfast made by the owner that reviews call tasty and generous. · Honest caveats from the reviews: the thing mentioned most is having to climb about 60 stairs from the road to the house, which is tough for anyone with heavy bags or who can't manage stairs. · Next is that it's in the island's center, not beachfront, so you'll need a motorbike; the furniture leans simple and not brand-new; and a minority of reviews ran into a room or a welcome that didn't quite hit the mark on occasion. · Best for couples and travelers willing to trade a little comfort for a view and atmosphere you won't find at this price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request a room with a sea-facing balcony at booking, because not every room has the same view. · Pack light, since you'll climb about 60 stairs, and rent a motorbike at the pier or have the owner help arrange one for getting around the island.
pros: Gulf of Thailand and sunset views from the cliff that reviews call among the prettiest on the island
Clean rooms, many with a private sea-facing balcony
Kind owner speaks German and English, looks after you like family · breakfast included
Great value for couples and solo travelers
cons: You have to climb about 60 stairs from the road to the stay
In the island's center, not beachfront — you'll need a motorbike or car
Small guesthouse, no swimming pool, simple furniture (per reviews)

entries.type: Garden Bungalow · garden bungalows in the island's center
entries.name: Charlie's Bungalows
entries.badge: 💛 Owner looks after you like family
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Thewawong · island center, near the pier
entries.addr: 39/2 Moo 2, Tha Thewawong Sub-district, Koh Sichang, Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: Charlie's Bungalows is one of the most talked-about stays on Koh Sichang — a set of 14 detached bungalows in a tropical garden run by the owner and family, sitting in the island's center in Tha Thewawong Sub-district. It scores as high as 9.7 on Trip.com from 44 reviews and around 4.4/5 on TripAdvisor. · It isn't a luxe beachfront resort, and it isn't a budget hostel in a shophouse — it's detached, private bungalows where you don't share a wall or walkway with anyone, set among a green, shady, quiet garden. · What reviews agree on most is that the rooms are very clean, the linens and towels are clean, and the construction is solid and looks new. Every bungalow is air-conditioned with a water heater, fridge, flat-screen TV, kettle with tea and coffee, and a private balcony to sit with a coffee looking at the garden morning or evening. · The service highlight is the owner and family who look after you like relatives — many reviews describe them as friendly and kind, helping with everything from picking you up at the pier to arranging a motorbike rental at around 300 baht a day with a full tank, to recommending restaurants, until you feel like a real guest rather than just a customer. · The in-village location is still within walking distance of restaurants and the market. · Honest caveats from the reviews: it isn't beachfront — Tham Phang Beach and Laem Phrommathep are on the other side, about a 5–10 minute motorbike ride away — the beds are fairly firm in the Thai style, there's too little shelf space in the rooms, there's no restaurant or breakfast on-site, and at times it's cash-only. · Best for those who want a simple, quiet Koh Sichang trip, riding a motorbike around the island, with a warm owner at a price you can reach.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Let them know your pier arrival time in advance to use the transfer, and book a motorbike rental ahead — especially on long weekends when the bikes can all be taken. · Bring enough cash, since at times the stays and shops on the island are cash-only.
pros: Detached bungalows that are clean and private, with a shady, quiet garden
Owner and family look after you like relatives, helping with everything (the point reviews praise most)
Motorbike rental and pier transfer make getting around easy
Island-center location, walk to restaurants and the market · good value
cons: Not beachfront — you'll need a motorbike to reach the beach on the other side
Beds fairly firm in the Thai style · no restaurant or breakfast on-site
Cash-only at times, no cards (per reviews)

entries.name: Adrian View Resort
entries.badge: 💰 Lowest starting price in the set
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Thewawong · near the Khao Khat viewpoint
tags: 🦋 Butterfly garden, every room has a balcony
entries.addr: 262/17 Moo 6, Tha Thewawong Sub-district, Koh Sichang, Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: If your budget isn't big but you want to escape the city for a quiet night on Koh Sichang, Adrian View Resort is the lowest starting price in this set at ฿800/night — a small Bed & Breakfast guesthouse of just about 7 rooms run by the owner, in Tha Thewawong Sub-district. It's been open since around 2012 and has built a base of repeat guests, scoring 8.5 on Trip.com and 4.3/5 on TripAdvisor (4th of the 11 Specialty stays on the island). · Its charm lies in being simple and friendly rather than luxurious. · What many people like is that every room has a private balcony or terrace with a small sitting nook to step out, catch the breeze, and sip coffee in the morning, decorated in bright, easy-on-the-eye colors rather than the bland look of typical budget guesthouses. Rooms have AC, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, and a private bathroom. · The common-area highlight is a small garden with butterflies fluttering about in the morning, a relaxing atmosphere, and a location near the Khao Khat viewpoint and Laem Chakkraphong, within about a 7-minute walk to the pier and the village — good for those not renting transport on the island. · Service draws heavy praise, with the owner or caretaker being friendly and recommending spots like staying at a friend's place. · Honest caveats from the reviews: the rooms are very simple with no frills or luxe amenities, the stay is small with no swimming pool or on-site activities, the name says "View" but not every room has a full wide sea view — many look onto the garden or surroundings — and the breakfast and amenities info on some booking channels doesn't match, so check directly with the owner. · Best for couples, solo travelers, and budget-minded folks who want quiet, cleanliness, and friendliness.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's a small owner-run stay, so call or message on Facebook to confirm availability, price, and breakfast as clearly as possible before booking. · If a view matters to you, ask specifically which room has the best one, since not every room has a wide sea view.
pros: Lowest starting price in the set at ฿800 · good value among budget stays
Small 7-room guesthouse, quiet and private, every room has a balcony
Relaxing butterfly garden, near the Khao Khat viewpoint, walk to the pier
Attentive owner like staying at a friend's place (the point reviews praise most)
cons: Rooms are very simple, no swimming pool or on-site activities
The name says "View" but not every room has a wide sea view
Breakfast info on some channels doesn't match — check with the owner first (per reviews)

entries.name: Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Thewawong · seaside on the island
tags: 🌊 Many rooms with wide sea-and-mountain-view balconies
🚲 Bike rental for exploring the island
entries.storyHtml: If you want to wake up to the sea on the island for a few thousand baht, Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang is a small seaside resort plenty of people mention — a small stay of about 16 rooms run by the owner, open since 2016, set by the sea in the Tha Thewawong area. It scores 7.5 from 60 reviews on Trip.com (location 7.8 · service 7.4). · It isn't a luxury resort with a private beach or an infinity pool, but it sells two things clearly: the seaside view on the island and a quiet atmosphere. · The rooms' selling point lives up to the name — many rooms open onto wide balconies with a full view of Koh Sichang's sea and mountains, and many reviews praise the fairly wide balconies as a comfortable place to sip coffee and take in the view. Rooms have AC, a fridge, free drinking water, and a private bathroom. · A consistent point of praise is the freshly made breakfast included in the room rate — some praise getting a morning meal with a sea view in a quiet setting — plus an on-site restaurant open for lunch and dinner, and the owner (Khun Santi) who looks after guests personally and attentively, helping recommend spots and call a ride, so that many people are willing to overlook the building's limitations. · Honest caveats from the reviews: the thing mentioned most is inconsistent room condition and cleanliness, with some reviews finding a broken bathroom door or details that need fixing; next is hot water that doesn't come consistently in some rooms, the room you get sometimes not matching the booking photos, a location fairly far from the shops requiring transport, and no swimming pool, gym, or spa. · Best for couples and small families wanting to escape the city for a quiet night by the sea, ready to set expectations for a small 2-star stay, not a luxury resort.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request a sea-view balcony room at booking, since it's the standout feature and makes a big difference to the atmosphere. · If you're worried about the hot water or room condition, contact the resort directly to ask before you travel for peace of mind.
pros: Many rooms with wide sea-and-mountain-view balconies to take in the view all day
Freshly made breakfast included in the rate + on-site restaurant
Owner (Khun Santi) looks after guests personally and attentively, helps recommend spots
Quiet atmosphere, good value among the island's stays
cons: Room condition and cleanliness aren't consistent across every room
Hot water in some rooms doesn't come consistently · no swimming pool
Location fairly far from the shops, requires transport (per reviews)

entries.name: Moroc Home Resort Koh Sichang
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Thewawong · near the pier, on a hill
entries.addr: 76 Moo 3, Tha Thewawong Sub-district, Koh Sichang, Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: Among Koh Sichang stays, if you want one with an atmosphere unlike the rest, Moroc Home Resort Koh Sichang is the choice that brings a Moroccan flavor to a small island — a small resort of about 18 rooms that was originally named Malee Blue, fully renovated before reopening as Moroc Home in 2015, set on a hill in Tha Thewawong Sub-district. It scores around 5.9 from 114 reviews on Agoda and 4.0 on TripAdvisor. · The main selling point that makes the place stick in your memory is the Moroccan-style decor playing with bold colors — orange, indigo, and white contrasting, with patterns and decorative pieces blending an Arabesque flavor with modern, turning nearly every corner into a photo backdrop. · The rooms are simple for the price, each with AC, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, and free Wi-Fi, and some corners of the resort look onto the sea and the cargo ships mid-bay. · Another positive surprise is the breakfast that many reviews say is done better than the price suggests — capable cooking, tasty pumpkin soup, and the option to add specific dishes like fish congee, plus a warm welcome from the owner and staff. · Honest caveats from the reviews: the thing mentioned most is that there's no swimming pool, which disappoints those who came intending to swim at the resort; next is room condition and some fittings starting to show their age since it's been open since 2015, with the polish and value that some reviews feel still falls short of expectations, keeping the overall score mid-range, plus you have to take the ferry across and then a skylab up the hill. · Best for couples, groups of friends, and photo-minded travelers who want a budget trip with an atmosphere that has character, using the resort as a base for getting around the island.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Know in advance there's no swimming pool — if you came to swim, plan to head to Tham Phang Beach instead. · If a sea view or a specific decorated corner matters to you, ask and specify the room type at booking, since each room's atmosphere and orientation differ.
pros: Bright Moroccan-style decor, photogenic and unlike anything else on the island
Breakfast done better than the price suggests, praised in many reviews
Budget price from ฿984, good for a one-night trip
Friendly welcome, small resort that feels close-knit
cons: No swimming pool — those who came to swim at the resort may be disappointed
Some rooms and fittings starting to show their age, overall score mid-range
You have to take the ferry across and then a skylab up the hill (per reviews)

entries.name: Sichang Palace
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Thewawong · town center, walk to the pier
tags: 📍 Town center, walk to the pier
🏊 Has a swimming pool on the island
entries.addr: 81 Moo 1, Tha Thewawong Sub-district, Koh Sichang, Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: Closing out with a choice that's "good value if you set your expectations right" — Sichang Palace is a three-story, 3-star hotel set in the middle of the Tha Thewawong village, looking out over the town of Koh Sichang, the bay, and the channel back toward the mainland. · To be honest, this is an older building that's been open a long time, so its score sits mid-range at 5.6 on Trip.com and 2.8 of 5 from 24 reviews on TripAdvisor — we placed it last because the physical condition is the main limitation guests should know first, but it still has strengths that many stays on the island can't offer. · Its biggest strength is the town-center location, being one of the few stays on the island where guests can walk to the pier, market, restaurants, and the skylab rental in just a few minutes without relying on a shuttle, and it's easy to head out for food in the evening. · Another point many reviews recommend is the front rooms with Juliette balconies facing the bay, good for waking up early to watch the sunrise and the cargo ships at sea, and the place has an outdoor pool and a kids' pool, which is rare among similarly priced stays on the island. · Amid the middling reviews about the building, the staff's service is actually the most consistently praised point — both Thai and foreign guests say they're friendly and more helpful than expected. · Honest caveats from the reviews: the building and decor are old with age, with many reviews saying it should be renovated, cleanliness in some rooms isn't consistent (some reviews found stains, carpet, or a musty smell), pool upkeep is inconsistent at times, the Wi-Fi is slow, and there's noise from the community and the mosque in the early morning. · Best for those wanting a town-center location, a budget price, the freedom to walk around and find food, plus a bay view from the front rooms — more than those wanting a polished new room or the deep quiet of escaping the city.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request a front room with a bay-facing balcony at booking, since the bay view is the most worthwhile highlight of the rooms here. · If you can, ask to see the room before check-in since the old building means each room's condition isn't consistent, and pack earplugs in case of community noise in the early morning.
pros: Town-center location, walk to the pier and restaurants without relying on a shuttle
Front rooms with bay-view balconies, good for watching the sunrise
Has a swimming pool and a kids' pool, which is rare on the island
Friendly, helpful staff · accessible starting price
cons: Building and decor are old with age, many reviews say it should be renovated
Cleanliness in some rooms isn't consistent · pool upkeep inconsistent at times, slow Wi-Fi
Noise from the community and the mosque in the early morning (per reviews)

adviceTitle: How do you pick a Koh Sichang stay that fits your trip?

advice.head: Want a seaside boutique, nice design, highest score
advice.bodyHtml: → Somewhere Koh Sichang ฿1,900, a blue-and-white Cape & Kantary-group boutique, balcony in every room, sea-view pool, free pier shuttle, score 9.6

advice.head: Want to watch the sunset from your room's balcony
advice.bodyHtml: → Koh Sichang Unseen ฿1,900, a clifftop bungalow, nearly every room faces the sea, with a private beach where you see the cave at low tide · or Yellow House ฿1,400, a yellow house on the cliffside

advice.head: Budget, want a clean bed, easy-to-walk location
advice.bodyHtml: → Benjaporn Bungalow ฿1,100, walk to the pier, free shuttle, free bike · or Adrian View ฿800, the cheapest in the set · or Charlie's Bungalows ฿930, bungalows in a garden

advice.head: Want an owner who looks after you like family
advice.bodyHtml: → Charlie's Bungalows ฿930, bungalows in a garden, motorbike rental for exploring the island · or Yellow House ฿1,400, owner speaks German and English, ready to recommend great spots

advice.head: Photo-minded, want an atmosphere unlike anything else
advice.bodyHtml: → Moroc Home Resort ฿984, bright Moroccan-style decor, breakfast draws praise (no swimming pool)

advice.head: Want a town-center location, walk around on your own
advice.bodyHtml: → Sichang Palace ฿1,000, town center, walk to the pier, has a swimming pool, front rooms with bay views (old building, set your expectations right)

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates from the standard room range and may change by date and season; we recommend checking the real price and comparing 3 sites before every booking. · The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms — we didn't stay ourselves. · Most stays on Koh Sichang are small (7–20 rooms/units), so they fill up fast; on long weekends and during the travel season, book ahead and check the last-ferry schedule carefully. · Getting there: take the ferry from Koh Loy Pier, Sriracha, about 45 minutes (fare around 50 baht); you don't need to bring a car onto the island — just park on the Sriracha side. · On the island, use a skylab or rent a motorbike to get around. · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travelers ask most about Koh Sichang stays

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best place to stay on Koh Sichang?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. · If you measure by score and design, Somewhere Koh Sichang has the highest score in the article at 9.6, a seaside boutique in the Cape & Kantary group. · If you focus on a sunset view from the balcony, Koh Sichang Unseen is a clifftop bungalow where nearly every room faces the sea. · If you measure by number of reviews and in-village value, Benjaporn Bungalow has the most reviews and is TripAdvisor #2 small stay on the island. · If you focus on an owner who looks after you like family, Charlie's Bungalows or Yellow House

faq.q: ❓ How much do Koh Sichang stays cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at about ฿800–1,900 per night. · The most budget end is Adrian View from ฿800, Charlie's Bungalows ฿930, and Moroc Home ฿984. · Mid-range is Sichang Palace ฿1,000, Benjaporn ฿1,100, Yellow House ฿1,400, and Ocean View ฿1,500. · The upper end is Somewhere and Koh Sichang Unseen from ฿1,900. · All prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms; on long weekends prices may be higher than usual

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Sichang · do you need to bring a car onto the island?
faq.a: Start by driving or taking a car to Koh Loy Pier, Sriracha (about 1.5–2 hours from Bangkok), then take the ferry that runs on set departures — the fare is around 50 baht and it takes about 45 minutes. · You don't need to bring your own car onto the island; just park on the Sriracha side — some stays like Somewhere and Koh Sichang Unseen have free parking on the Sriracha side. · On the island, use a skylab or rent a motorbike to get around

faq.q: ❓ Which Koh Sichang stay is good for couples?
faq.a: Most stays on the island lean toward a quiet atmosphere that suits couples. · The standouts for view and design are Somewhere Koh Sichang, a blue-and-white boutique with sea views from every room's balcony, and Koh Sichang Unseen, where you can watch the sunset from your room's balcony. · If you like a small, warm, owner-run house, Yellow House, Charlie's Bungalows, and Adrian View are lovely choices on a lighter budget

faq.q: ❓ Which Koh Sichang stays have a swimming pool?
faq.a: There aren't many stays on Koh Sichang with a swimming pool. · In this article, Somewhere Koh Sichang has an outdoor sea-view pool, and Sichang Palace has an outdoor pool and a kids' pool (though some reviews say pool upkeep is inconsistent at times, so check the condition on arrival). · Koh Sichang Unseen, Yellow House, Charlie's, Adrian View, Moroc Home, and Benjaporn have no swimming pool, focusing on sea views and atmosphere instead. · Anyone wanting a full swim usually heads to Tham Phang Beach on the island

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a Koh Sichang stay?
faq.a: Most stays on Koh Sichang are small (7–20 rooms/units, some just 7 rooms), so they fill up fast. · During long weekends, festivals, and weekends, book 2–4 weeks ahead or more, since Bangkok folks favor staying then and rooms sell out quickly. · On weekdays, booking a few days ahead is enough. · Every platform usually offers Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in a price if your plans aren't set, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best rate. · And don't forget to check the last-ferry schedule back carefully
